channel.title: Daily Recap — 📟Tech News
channel.description: What happened in 📟Tech News, recapped daily from subscribed feeds.

item.title: Trump wants Tim Cook to run Nvidia as tech leaders react to Huang's resignation
item.description:
Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO following reports of two affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy and one with a direct report, and the company is now led on an interim basis by CFO Colette Kress. President Donald Trump is already pushing a successor: former Apple CEO Tim Cook, now Apple's chairman.

Tech leaders reacting to the resignation called it a mistake, reflecting how central Huang was to the AI era — he built Nvidia into the most important company in computing. The succession question now looms over the chipmaker, with Trump's public lobbying adding a political dimension to what would already be one of the most consequential CEO searches in tech.

Sources

  • The Verge: Donald Trump really wants Tim Cook to run Nvidia
  • The Verge: ‘It’s a mistake’: reactions from tech leaders on Jensen Huang’s resignation

item.title: Google's new Gemini model tackles your most complicated Search questions
item.description:
Google says its new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model gives more helpful answers to complex questions, including ones with multiple parts, hard-to-understand typos, or highly specific requests. The model breaks questions down and addresses each part in its responses.

It's available starting today in Search, the Gemini app, and across Google's tiers. The upgrade is part of Google's push to make AI Mode in Search the place for hard questions rather than simple lookups — a direct answer to AI chatbots that have been eating into traditional search.

Sources

  • The Verge: Google’s new Gemini model is better at understanding complicated questions

item.title: Microsoft Outlook suffers a global outage
item.description:
Outlook went down just before 1PM ET on Thursday, with users around the world unable to access email through the web or apps. Microsoft acknowledged the issue from its Microsoft 365 Status account, saying a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions.

The outage hit one of the world's most widely used email services during the workday, leaving businesses and individuals locked out of their inboxes. As of the latest update, Microsoft was still working on a fix, with no cause given beyond the infrastructure strain.

Sources

  • The Verge: Microsoft Outlook is still down

item.title: Nvidia privately said chip tracking to fight smuggling is possible
item.description:
Nvidia representatives told Representative Bill Foster that it would be technically possible to implement the anti-smuggling measures called for in the Chip Security Act, Foster told MIT Technology Review — even while an industry group publicly claimed the measures were potentially infeasible.

The gap between Nvidia's private and public positions matters: location verification and tracking for advanced chips is a key tool Congress wants to stop smuggling to China, and industry resistance has been a major obstacle. Foster, a Democrat on the House intelligence committee, says the company confirmed the technology is workable, undercutting the argument that the law asks for the impossible.

Sources

  • MIT Technology Review: Nvidia privately confirmed it could track chips to fight smuggling, even as industry publicly questioned feasibility

item.title: Whoop launches a social network built on verified health data
item.description:
Whoop launched Whoop Humans, a social network where members share data from their wearables — sleep, recovery, and workout metrics — alongside Story-like Moments with photos and captions, plus comments and reactions. The company claims the platform is entirely human, with every user backed by a verified heartbeat.

The bigger bet is turning Whoop from a tracker into a personal health brand, with CEO Will Ahmed hinting at acquisitions to come. It's an unusual social play: rather than competing on content, Whoop is competing on authenticity, using real biometric data as proof that the people — and the achievements — are genuine.

Sources

  • The Verge: Whoop launched a social network where every user has a ‘verified heartbeat’

item.title: Xbox announces Wolfenstein 3 and brings 25 original Xbox games to PC
item.description:
Xbox had a big day for fans of its history. Bethesda's MachineGames officially announced Wolfenstein 3, nearly a decade after Wolfenstein II: The New Colossus in 2017 — and just days after Bethesda confirmed the next Elder Scrolls will be called The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel.

For the 25th anniversary of Xbox, Microsoft also began making 25 original Xbox games playable on Windows PC, as long as you own (or buy) digital copies — the start of its paid next-gen game preservation promise. And Xbox Insiders began testing new dashboard customizations, including rotating backgrounds and a movable Guide menu. Together, it's a nostalgia-heavy push as Xbox leans on its back catalog.

Sources

  • The Verge: Xbox announces Wolfenstein 3
  • The Verge: Here are the 25 original Xbox games you can now play on PC
  • The Verge: Xbox owners are getting more customizations for backgrounds and the Guide menu

item.title: Humble Bundle redesign quietly removes two-factor verification settings
item.description:
Humble Bundle's redesigned storefront no longer offers a way to add or update two-factor verification methods on its settings page, as reported by Kotaku. Support pages still discuss two-factor verification, but the option itself appears to have vanished in the redesign.

It's a concerning regression for a store that holds users' payment details and game libraries: removing a security control, even accidentally, leaves accounts more exposed. Whether the removal was intentional or an oversight of the redesign, Humble Bundle has not yet explained it — and users who relied on 2FA now have no way to manage it.

Sources

  • The Verge: Humble Bundle redesign removes two-factor verification from settings

item.title: Nvidia board reportedly preparing to fire Jensen Huang
item.description:
Nvidia's board is preparing to dismiss CEO Jensen Huang following a report from the New York Times about a second alleged extramarital affair, just days after he admitted to a separate affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy, according to the Wall Street Journal. The second alleged affair was with an executive.

Huang is one of the most prominent CEOs in tech, having built Nvidia into the indispensable supplier of AI chips and one of the world's most valuable companies. A board move against him would be a seismic leadership event with immediate implications for Nvidia's strategy, its relationships with the big AI labs, and the stock market — though the reports remain unconfirmed, and the board has not publicly commented.

Sources

  • The Verge: Nvidia is reportedly preparing to fire Jensen Huang

item.title: United won't let your AI agent book your flight
item.description:
United Airlines says it won't let personal AI assistants book tickets on the airline, citing both privacy and regulatory concerns. The company says it hasn't yet seen many people try to use AI agents to book flights — in line with observations from other businesses like DoorDash — but it is drawing the line preemptively.

The move is an early sign of how established companies are responding to agentic AI: rather than waiting for AI assistants to become a booking channel, United is blocking them on principle. The tension is only going to grow as personal agents get more capable — travelers may soon expect their assistant to handle bookings, while airlines and other merchants worry about losing control of the customer relationship, pricing, and the personal data that flows through a purchase.

Sources

  • The Verge: United won’t let your AI agent book your flight

item.title: EU's Digital Fairness Act takes aim at loot boxes, influencers, and addictive design
item.description:
Gaming, social media, and e-commerce platforms are facing a fresh wave of sweeping European Union rules aimed at making "your online experience fairer." The newly proposed Digital Fairness Act, published by the EU Commission on Wednesday, targets practices that push consumers into spending more of their time and money online — including loot boxes, influencer marketing, and addictive interface features.

The proposal is still early-stage, but it continues the EU's pattern of setting the global pace on tech regulation, from the GDPR to the Digital Markets Act. If it becomes law, platforms will have to rethink some of their most profitable engagement mechanics — and, as with past EU rules, the changes are likely to ripple well beyond Europe as companies standardize on the stricter standard.

Sources

  • The Verge: Loot boxes, influencers, and addictive features face an EU crackdown

item.title: Google's AlphaGenome 2 zooms in on the cellular roots of disease
item.description:
Researchers at Google DeepMind have unveiled AlphaGenome 2, a new AI model designed to unravel how changes in DNA affect different cells — giving scientists a more detailed view of a notoriously difficult problem that could hold important clues to the causes of disease and point the way to new treatments. It is the successor to the original AlphaGenome.

Understanding how a genetic variant behaves in one cell type but not another is central to making sense of the genome: the same mutation can be harmless in one tissue and disease-causing in another. A model that predicts those cell-specific effects could accelerate everything from drug target discovery to understanding rare genetic disorders.

Sources

  • The Verge: Google’s AlphaGenome 2 zooms in on the cellular roots of disease

item.title: Toyota brings back Scion — starting with a 25-mph kei truck built in Indiana
item.description:
Toyota is dusting off the Scion badge for a radically different mission. Rather than targeting youth-market hatchbacks, "Scion by Toyota" is being positioned as an experimental mobility incubator — and its first vehicle is an authentic Japanese-style kei truck built in Indiana, with a top speed of 25 mph.

Kei vehicles, built to satisfy Japan's light vehicle regulations, are enjoying a surge of interest in the US as compact, practical work trucks. A 25-mph top speed puts the truck squarely in low-speed-vehicle territory — farm, campus, and neighborhood use rather than highway driving — but as a first experiment for a revived Scion, it's a deliberately odd and attention-grabbing choice that signals Toyota is willing to test unconventional ideas under the badge.

Sources

  • The Verge: Toyota’s Scion is back, starting with an American-made, 25-mph kei truck

item.title: Hands on: Home Assistant's new Connect Aux-2 smart home multi-tool
item.description:
Nabu Casa — the commercial side of the Open Home Foundation, which runs Home Assistant — has launched the Home Assistant Connect Aux-2, a multi-function box designed to bring more non-smart devices into your smart home. It's part of Home Assistant's ongoing effort to become more user-friendly, and in hands-on testing, that effort appears to be working.

The Aux-2 matters because the smart home's biggest barrier has never been the gadgets — it's the long tail of ordinary devices that don't speak any smart-home protocol. A box that bridges that gap, from an open-source ecosystem that doesn't lock users into one vendor's cloud, is a meaningful step toward a smart home that normal people can actually set up and live with.

Sources

  • The Verge: Hands on with Home Assistant’s new ‘smart home multi-tool’

item.title: Google's Tabletop AI experiment builds custom collaboration apps for you
item.description:
Google has unveiled Tabletop, an experimental AI tool that generates customized collaborative hubs to help you coordinate with family and friends. The platform shares some visual similarities with workplace management apps like Asana and Monday, but with a built-in AI feature that lets you "vibecode" personalized interactive tools by describing what you need.

Tabletop is the latest in Google's string of AI experiments that turn natural-language descriptions into working software — this time aimed at the everyday coordination problems (family schedules, trip planning, shared chores) that existing apps handle only generically. It's available via waitlist, and like most Google experiments, its long-term future is uncertain — but the direction is clear: bespoke apps generated on demand, rather than one-size-fits-all software.

Sources

  • The Verge: Google’s Tabletop AI experiment lets you build custom collaboration apps

item.title: COP31 climate talks kick off in Turkey
item.description:
Thousands of delegates, lobbyists, and journalists have gathered for the annual UN climate talks, this year in Antalya, Turkey. COP31 officially kicked off on November 8, marking the beginning of negotiations on one of the biggest stages of the climate world, with Turkey and Australia cohosting.

The talks come at a fraught moment for global climate action, with negotiations over emissions targets, climate finance, and adaptation all on the agenda. For the tech world, the talks matter too: data centers, AI energy demand, and the clean-energy buildout are increasingly central to the climate conversation, and the outcomes in Antalya will shape the policy environment those industries operate in.

Sources

  • MIT Technology Review: What to know about this year’s UN climate talks

item.title: Microsoft's DLSS rival Auto SR rolls out for Xbox Ally X and Copilot+ PCs
item.description:
Microsoft's answer to Nvidia's DLSS is officially out. Automatic Super Resolution (Auto SR), an AI upscaling technology that boosts frame rates by rendering games at lower resolution and intelligently upscaling them, is now rolling out for the Xbox Ally X, the Xbox Ally X20, and select Windows Copilot+ PCs — with new features added alongside the launch.

Auto SR has been in testing since April, and the official release matters most for handheld gaming: on a device like the Ally X, upscaling is the difference between smooth play and a slideshow in demanding titles. The rollout also signals Microsoft's broader bet that AI upscaling belongs on Windows, not just on consoles — and that it can compete with DLSS on its home turf.

Sources

  • The Verge: Microsoft’s DLSS competitor is out for the Xbox Ally X and works in handheld mode

item.title: Disney Plus brings 60+ 3D movies to Meta Quest
item.description:
Disney is bringing more than 60 3D movies to the Disney Plus app on Meta Quest. The updated app, rolling out now, lets subscribers watch films like The Avengers and Black Panther in stereoscopic 3D inside VR — a catalog that turns the Quest into a personal 3D theater.

It's a meaningful content play for Meta's headset: 3D movies were one of the original promises of VR headsets, but the catalog has been thin. Disney's library is exactly the kind of marquee content that makes the feature feel real rather than a demo. For Quest owners with a Disney Plus subscription, the update is free and available today.

Sources

  • The Verge: The VR Disney Plus app on Meta Quest now has 3D movies

item.title: Oura acquires medical AI chatbot Counsel Health for $625 million
item.description:
Oura is going deeper into health AI. The smart-ring company announced it has agreed to acquire Counsel Health, an AI-native primary care startup, for $625 million. Counsel's AI chatbot was already integrated into Oura's app earlier this year, delivering AI-generated responses and insights based on users' reported health data.

The deal, announced alongside Oura's quarterly earnings, signals where wearables are heading: from tracking metrics to interpreting them — and increasingly, to offering something that resembles primary care. A $625 million acquisition is a big bet that users want their ring to do more than count steps; they want it to tell them what their data means and what to do about it. The regulatory and privacy questions around AI health advice are the obvious next chapter.

Sources

  • The Verge: Oura is acquiring medical AI chatbot startup Counsel Health

item.title: Sony cancels Fairgames and shuts down the PlayStation Plus PC app
item.description:
Sony is trimming its PlayStation ambitions on two fronts. The company has canceled Fairgames, the heist shooter announced in 2023 that was meant to anchor its big live-service push, according to Bloomberg. It's the latest casualty of that strategy: Sony has already canceled planned live-service titles in the God of War and The Last of Us franchises and shut down Concord after its disastrous launch.

Separately, Sony is retiring the PlayStation Plus app for PC on December 10. The app let Premium subscribers stream games on PC, but Sony says very few people used it. Together, the two moves paint a picture of a company narrowing its focus: fewer live-service bets, fewer side apps, and a retreat from experiments that didn't find an audience.

Sources

  • The Verge: Sony cancels live-service shooter Fairgames
  • The Verge: The PlayStation Plus PC app is shutting down next month

item.title: Starlink Mini 2 adds a swappable battery for $999
item.description:
SpaceX has a new version of its portable satellite internet terminal. The Starlink Mini 2 integrates the dish, Wi-Fi router, and now a battery into a single laptop-sized device — and the battery is swappable, so users can hot-swap in a fresh one for longer off-grid sessions.

The dish is priced at $999, according to order invitations shared by users, which includes the battery. The original Mini was already popular with travelers, RVers, and remote workers; adding a built-in battery removes the last tether — no more hunting for a power outlet to get online. It's a niche product at a premium price, but for people who work from genuinely anywhere, it's a compelling one.

Sources

  • The Verge: Starlink Mini 2 adds a swappable battery

item.title: Google's Pixel Tag tracker is now available
item.description:
Google's answer to the AirTag is finally on sale. The Pixel Tag, first announced in August, is now available — Google's own tracker designed for its Find Hub network and app. It uses ultra-wideband and Bluetooth, and it's priced similarly to Apple's AirTag.

The significance is less about the hardware than the ecosystem: Android has relied on third-party trackers from Samsung, Motorola, and Pebblebee for years, with mixed results. A first-party Google tracker, tightly integrated with the Find Hub network, should make finding lost items on Android as seamless as it is on iPhone. Whether it catches up to AirTag's network scale is the open question.

Sources

  • The Verge: Google’s Pixel Tag tracker is now available

item.title: Bambu Lab P2S Combo is $100 off through December 1
item.description:
One of the best-regarded multi-filament 3D printers is $100 off. The Bambu Lab P2S Combo is $649 — down from $749 — at Best Buy and directly from Bambu Lab, with the sale running through December 1.

The P2S is the enclosed CoreXY printer with an AMS multi-material system that has become the go-to recommendation for hassle-free printing: fewer filament jams, fewer clogged nozzles, and an enclosed chamber that handles a wider range of materials. At $649, it's the lowest price the Combo has seen, and the December 1 end date gives shoppers a few weeks to decide.

Sources

  • The Verge: One of our favorite multi-filament 3D printers is $100 off

item.title: Pelosi's successor heads to Washington ready to regulate AI
item.description:
AI regulation is moving from statehouse theory to congressional reality. Scott Wiener — the California state senator who authored legislation aimed at curbing the risks of advanced AI — has won Nancy Pelosi's House seat, and he's arriving in Washington ready to regulate. That's the headline of today's MIT Technology Review Download, and it signals a shift: AI's most prominent state-level regulator now has a federal platform.

The same edition flags the other side of the AI boom: data centers are running into power constraints and local backlash as their energy demands grow. Together, the two stories capture the moment — AI's political and physical infrastructure are both hitting limits at the same time, and the next Congress will have to deal with both.

Sources

  • MIT Technology Review: The Download: Pelosi’s successor targets AI and data centers face power woes

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admits affair with suspected Chinese informant as board opens investigation
item.description:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has acknowledged an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed, an AI compute company that rents access to Nvidia hardware. US intelligence reports had identified her since last year as a suspected Chinese informant, and Nvidia's board has opened an investigation into the matter. President Trump fielded questions about the scandal at a White House press briefing, saying he had only recently learned of it.

The episode lands at the worst possible moment for Nvidia, whose chips are the bedrock of the US AI buildout and whose CEO has been lobbying hard against tighter export controls on AI chips to China. With a newly elected Democratic Congress poised to scrutinize chip smuggling and push for stricter restrictions, the scandal hands Huang's critics fresh leverage — and raises uncomfortable questions about what access or influence Beijing may have gained through the relationship.

Sources

  • The Verge: Everything we know so far about the Nvidia spy scandal targeting CEO Jensen Huang
  • The Verge: Here's what Trump said he knew about Jensen Huang
  • The Verge: What could China get from Jensen Huang?

item.title: Anthropic launches Claude Fable and Mythos 5.2, its most powerful models yet
item.description:
Anthropic has released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, which it describes as its most powerful models to date, with improvements in coding, reasoning, vision, and output speed over the 5.1 versions. The company says the models can solve open physics problems, design functioning operating systems, and now write more than 90 percent of the code changes merged into Anthropic's own core codebase.

The launch comes in two tiers — one freely available, one reserved for verified organizations — and Anthropic says it deliberately curbed capabilities that would let the AI accelerate its own development. The timing matters: the release lands just before Anthropic's IPO, cementing its pitch as the frontier lab with the strongest coding models.

Sources

  • The Verge: Anthropic launches new Claude Fable and Mythos 5.2 models

item.title: At the UN climate summit, the pledge to use AI for climate good rings hollow
item.description:
As countries meet in Antalya, Turkey for the UN climate conference, the host has called on nations to commit to AI that is designed, powered, and deployed in ways that support climate action. But critics say the pledge is a cruel joke: the AI industry's data-center buildout is driving a surge in electricity demand, and the climate case for AI itself has not been made.

Former California Air Resources Board chair Mary Nichols argues in a new op-ed that the industry has yet to show AI's climate benefits outweigh its enormous energy footprint. The clash captures a growing tension — AI is pitched as a tool to fight climate change even as its infrastructure becomes one of the fastest-growing sources of new power demand.

Sources

  • The Verge: The global pledge to use AI for climate good is a cruel joke
  • MIT Technology Review: The climate case for AI has not been made

item.title: The data-center backlash might really just be about electricity
item.description:
Reporting from Ashburn, Virginia — the heart of Data Center Alley, the world's largest data-center hub — MIT Technology Review finds that voter anger about data centers may boil down to one thing: electricity. As Americans went to the polls last week, the costs landing on household power bills and the strain on the grid loomed larger than the usual concerns about water use or noise.

That reframes the politics of the AI buildout. If the backlash is fundamentally about who pays for power, the fight shifts from zoning boards to utility regulators and rate design — and the industry's promise to absorb its own costs will be tested in the bills voters actually see.

Sources

  • MIT Technology Review: The backlash about data centers might really just be about electricity

item.title: Apple starts charging $50 for extra Apple Intelligence usage
item.description:
Apple has begun selling one-time $49.99 "Intelligence Usage Packs" that extend access to some Apple Intelligence features. The option first appeared in Logic Pro, where users can now "Buy More Usage" to keep using its built-in AI assistant for tasks like starting songs and setting up sessions.

The packs follow a support article Apple published in early September outlining usage limits for certain Apple Intelligence features. It's a notable shift: Apple Intelligence was sold as part of the device, and now heavy users of its AI tools will hit a meter — with a paid top-up as the way past it.

Sources

  • The Verge: Apple's $50 Intelligence Usage Packs extend access to some AI features

item.title: Instagram's new Effect Builder generates custom filters from AI prompts
item.description:
Instagram has launched Effect Builder, a tool that creates custom filters for Stories from a text prompt, with an option to attach a style reference. It's available now to US users over 18, and it's the latest step in Meta's push to put generative AI directly into its creation tools.

The launch follows last week's expansion of Instagram's Edits app to macOS, and it fits a broader pattern: social platforms are racing to make AI-assisted creation a default part of posting, not a separate app. The open question is whether prompt-made filters become a genuine creative tool or just another novelty that fades after the first few tries.

Sources

  • The Verge: Instagram's Effect Builder makes new filters from AI prompts

item.title: Paramount's David Ellison calls AI the 'biggest creative unlock in modern history'
item.description:
On Paramount Skydance's latest earnings call, CEO David Ellison said AI could be the "biggest creative unlock in modern history" for filmmaking — and that it's "hard to imagine" its impact on the film industry won't exceed even CGI. The comment came in response to a question about the company's outlook for AI in production.

Ellison's framing signals where a major studio sees the technology heading: not just a cost-cutting tool, but a fundamental shift in how films get made. As studios weigh AI's promise against the creative community's skepticism, expect Paramount to lean in publicly — and for the debate over AI-generated content to keep intensifying.

Sources

  • The Verge: David Ellison says AI could be the 'biggest creative unlock in modern history'

item.title: Nvidia investigates CEO Jensen Huang over relationship with alleged Chinese spy
item.description:
Nvidia's board announced an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, an executive at Chinese firm Megaspeed who was reportedly recruited by China's Ministry of State Security to spy on the company. Huang sent a memo to Nvidia employees acknowledging the affair, the full text of which The Verge published.

The stakes are enormous: Nvidia is the most valuable company in the world and the linchpin of the global AI chip supply chain, and any compromise at the top raises questions about what information may have been exposed and how long the board knew. The investigation is just beginning, so the key unknowns — what was shared, and when — remain unanswered.

Sources

  • The Verge: Nvidia is investigating Jensen Huang’s relationship with a Chinese spy
  • The Verge: Here’s the full text of Jensen Huang’s memo to Nvidia

item.title: Apple races to make Siri a true AI agent
item.description:
Apple CEO John Ternus is reportedly pressuring AI chief Craig Federighi to accelerate Siri's roadmap and deliver a powerful AI agent that can compete with OpenAI's Dots and Meta's Muse. Federighi has already shipped a functional version of Siri AI on a tight timeline, but Apple has no illusions that it yet matches its rivals.

This is Apple's latest attempt to close the gap after years of falling behind on AI assistants. The pressure from the top suggests Siri's agentic upgrade is now a company-level priority, though there's still no public timeline for when the more capable version will arrive.

Sources

  • The Verge: Apple is racing to make Siri more agentic

item.title: Elvis and Eminem rights holders sue Suno over AI music clones
item.description:
AI music company Suno faces two new lawsuits: rights holders for Elvis Presley's music and the publisher of some of Eminem's biggest records allege Suno illegally generates music and lyrics that mimic those artists. The Presley suit invokes Tennessee's publicity-rights protections, among other claims.

Suno is already fighting multiple copyright cases, and these add two of the most recognizable names in music to the list. The suits are another test of where the line sits between AI-generated music inspired by an artist and unlawful imitation of their voice, style, and lyrics.

Sources

  • The Verge: Elvis and Eminem rights holders are suing Suno

item.title: Epic Games Launcher is coming to SteamOS
item.description:
Epic Games has confirmed its launcher is coming to SteamOS, Valve's Linux-based operating system, along with a handful of other Linux distributions. The news follows Epic saying in October that it was investigating making Fortnite compatible with SteamOS.

The move matters because SteamOS is expanding beyond the Steam Deck, and Epic's presence would make the platform a more credible home for PC gaming outside Windows. It also signals a thaw in the long-running Epic–Valve standoff over storefronts, though there's no word yet on when the launcher will actually ship.

Sources

  • The Verge: Epic Games Launcher is coming to SteamOS

item.title: Chatbots may be coming to Apple's HomeView hub
item.description:
Code in the iOS 27.3 beta suggests Apple could add chatbot support to its smart home hub, with a flag for a "Conversational Apps" category. No specific apps are named, but AI chatbots like ChatGPT and Claude are the obvious candidates.

If it ships, it would put third-party AI assistants on Apple's home hardware for the first time — a notable opening for a company that has historically kept its platforms tightly controlled. For now it's only a code flag, so the feature may or may not make the final release.

Sources

  • The Verge: Chatbots might be coming to Apple’s HomeView

item.title: Tesla is winding down the Cybertruck
item.description:
Elon Musk announced early Friday morning that Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production next year to make room for the Cybercab, effectively killing the vehicle less than three years after launch. The announcement came by tweet in the middle of the night — a notably unceremonious end for a truck once hailed as the future of Tesla.

The Cybertruck never lived up to its hype: production volumes stayed low, and its polarizing design and Musk's politics made it a lightning rod. Its demise frees up factory capacity for the Cybercab, Tesla's autonomous robotaxi bet, but it also closes the book on one of the most talked-about vehicle launches of the decade — a reminder that even Tesla can't will a niche product into a mass-market hit.

Sources

  • The Verge: Good riddance, Cybertruck!

item.title: US let Nvidia sell AI chips to an empty office in China
item.description:
The Commerce Department approved a Chinese firm called New Matrix to receive Nvidia's powerful H200 AI chips — despite the company's offices being, in the words of a New York Times report, "a hollow gray shell." The revelation raises serious questions about whether either the government or Nvidia is doing real due diligence on the firms cleared to handle advanced AI hardware.

The H200 is among the most capable AI accelerators on the market, and export controls are supposed to keep it out of the hands of unvetted or shell entities in China. If approved buyers turn out to be empty offices, the controls look less like a wall and more like a formality — and the episode is likely to fuel calls for tighter vetting of every firm on the approved list.

Sources

  • The Verge: The US let Nvidia sell chips to an empty office in China

item.title: Anthropic is using AI to build better AI — twice as fast as last year
item.description:
A new report from AI safety research group METR, based on an 11-week investigation, finds Anthropic is using AI systems to accelerate its own AI development — and it's working remarkably well. The company's models are now improving roughly twice as quickly as they were a year ago, with little sign of slowing down.

The findings are alarming researchers because they suggest the AI development loop is starting to feed on itself: smarter models build still smarter models, compressing timelines that safety researchers assumed would be much longer. If the trend holds across the industry, the window for figuring out how to govern and control advanced AI could be far shorter than anyone planned for.

Sources

  • The Verge: Why a new report on Anthropic automating AI development is alarming researchers

item.title: AI has broken cybersecurity — and nobody knows what's next
item.description:
In a new Verge podcast episode, longtime security expert Alex Stamos — now chief security officer at Cognition — argues that AI has fundamentally broken the cybersecurity world as we knew it. Attackers can now move faster and at greater scale than defenders, and the old playbook of patching and monitoring can't keep up.

Stamos's warning lands at a moment when AI-powered attacks are already reshaping the threat landscape, from automated phishing to AI-assisted vulnerability discovery. The open question is what replaces the old model: security teams will need AI of their own, new architectures, and possibly a rethink of how much trust any system deserves by default. The episode is the first in a series on AI in real life.

Sources

  • The Verge: AI broke the cybersecurity world. What's next?

item.title: NYT Cooking's AI assistant is great at chicken, nearly disastrous at cake
item.description:
The New York Times Cooking app's new AI assistant is a genuinely useful weeknight companion — until it isn't. In a hands-on review, it rescued a weeknight chicken dinner with smart, practical substitutions and timing help, turning a familiar rut into something the household actually enjoyed.

But the same assistant nearly ruined a cake, offering advice that would have derailed the bake. The split verdict captures where cooking AI stands today: strong on improvisation and weeknight problem-solving, shakier on precision tasks where one wrong instruction wastes an hour of work and a batch of ingredients. Useful, but worth double-checking before you trust it with dessert.

Sources

  • The Verge: NYT Cooking's AI assistant saved my weeknight chicken, but almost ruined my cake

item.title: A UV-tracking necklace that changes how you think about sunlight
item.description:
The90's Gem necklace tracks UV exposure throughout the day, and a hands-on review found it reframed sunlight as a health issue, not just a cosmetic one. Sitting under a patio umbrella with a fan at an outdoor party in 90-degree Los Angeles heat, the reviewer still felt exhausted and dizzy within half an hour — a reminder that shade and breeze don't block UV.

The Gem's appeal is that it makes invisible exposure visible, nudging wearers to reapply sunscreen or move indoors before they feel the effects. It's a small, focused wearable in a market full of do-everything devices, and its value is less about the hardware than the habit change it prompts.

Sources

  • The Verge: The UV-tracking Gem made me rethink how sunlight affects my health, not just my appearance

item.title: Zelda's Ocarina of Time remake is here — and Costco has it for $5 off
item.description:
The remastered Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is out for Switch 2, and early impressions say the classic holds up beautifully in its new form. The Verge's Installer newsletter puts it at the top of the week's recommendations, calling the return of the 1998 landmark a highlight of the season.

If you missed the preorder discounts, there's still a small saving to be had: Costco members can get $5 off the digital version, bringing it to $54.99. It's a modest discount on a $60 game, but for a title this anticipated, any saving counts — and the remake's arrival is the bigger story either way.

  • The Verge: Zelda is back and better than ever
  • The Verge: Costco members can get $5 off the reimagined Ocarina of Time

item.title: OpenAI now valued at $1.25 trillion after another $11 billion raise
item.description:
OpenAI has raised another $11 billion at a valuation of $1.25 trillion, according to Bloomberg, putting it among the most valuable companies in the world. The jump is striking even by OpenAI's own recent standards: it raised $122 billion in March at an $852 billion valuation, meaning the company has added roughly $400 billion in paper value in about eight months.

The timing matters because the broader tech market just took a sharp hit, with trillions wiped off valuations in a single day. OpenAI raising at a record price while rival Anthropic struggles to get its own IPO over the line suggests investors are drawing a sharp line between the AI leader and everyone else — or that the AI funding boom is concentrating at the very top.

Sources

  • The Verge: OpenAI valued at $1.25 trillion, as rival Anthropic nears its IPO

item.title: China reportedly recruited an AI executive to spy on Nvidia's Jensen Huang
item.description:
China's Ministry of State Security recruited Megaspeed executive Alice Huang to spy on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, according to The New York Times. The goal was to gather information about American AI chips and potentially push Nvidia to make its most advanced chips available to China.

The report lands at the center of the US-China chip war, where export controls on Nvidia's top accelerators have become one of Washington's main levers. If the allegation holds, it shows Beijing's intelligence efforts reaching directly into the executive orbit of the single most important company in the AI hardware supply chain — and raises fresh questions about how exposed the industry's leadership is to that pressure.

Sources

  • The Verge: China reportedly recruited AI exec to spy on Jensen Huang

item.title: SpaceX wants Starlink Mobile to become a major US carrier
item.description:
SpaceX has declared it intends to turn Starlink Mobile into a “major” mobile carrier, aiming to rival AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile. The company has already deployed thousands of direct-to-cell satellites, and has now signed deals to build out the terrestrial side of the business — the 5G network on Earth that a real carrier needs.

Satellite-to-phone service has so far been a niche add-on for dead zones, but SpaceX is clearly aiming bigger: a full-service carrier built on its space infrastructure. The open question is whether it can assemble the spectrum, towers, and regulatory approvals to compete with incumbents that spent decades building theirs.

Sources

  • The Verge: Starlink Mobile: All the news on SpaceX’s major mobile carrier ambitions

item.title: AI data centers keep colliding with power grids, bills, and local communities
item.description:
The race to build massive AI data centers is running into the physical limits of the power grid — and the political limits of the communities hosting them. The energy-hungry server warehouses have become a major bipartisan issue, with fights breaking out over their impact on utility bills, local power supplies, and the environment.

Data centers are the physical foundation of every AI company's ambitions, so the buildout isn't slowing down. But the backlash is now shaping policy: permitting, grid capacity, and who pays for the extra electricity are becoming central questions in the AI boom, not side issues.

Sources

  • The Verge: All the latest updates on AI data centers

item.title: Lame-duck Congress may actually speed up energy projects
item.description:
A major permitting-reform bill that could help energy projects come online much faster — and potentially lower utility bills — is advancing in Congress with bipartisan support. The bill would cut red tape for new power infrastructure, which has become a bottleneck as data centers demand ever more electricity.

The catch is that faster permitting cuts both ways: it could accelerate clean energy projects, but also polluting ones, and it would limit oversight of new data centers. Still, the fact that a lame-duck Congress is moving on it at all signals how much the energy crunch has become a shared political priority.

Sources

  • The Verge: Lame-duck Congress might actually do something: speed up energy projects

item.title: Someone at the White House appears to be running a rentable residential proxy
item.description:
Security researchers at Layer3 Intel and Synthient discovered residential proxy activity on the White House network, meaning outsiders could apparently rent access that routes their traffic through presidential IP addresses for just a few dollars, according to reporting by Krebs on Security and The Register.

Residential proxies are commonly used to disguise the origin of web traffic, and an exit node inside the White House network would be a prized asset for anyone wanting to look like a trusted US government user. How the software got there — and whether it was installed deliberately or through compromise — remains unclear.

Sources

  • The Verge: Just about anyone can rent access to White House IP addresses

item.title: I watched a humanoid robot clean my apartment
item.description:
A new humanoid-robot cleaning service in San Francisco sent a robot to clean a reviewer's apartment, and the experience felt like a genuine glimpse of the future — not a demo, but a working service doing real housework in a real home.

Humanoid robots have mostly lived in lab videos and trade-show demos, so a commercial cleaning service is a meaningful step: it means the hardware is reliable enough, and the economics plausible enough, to sell to ordinary customers. It's still early — one city, one service — but it's the kind of mundane, practical deployment that usually signals a technology is starting to cross over from promise to product.

  • MIT Technology Review: I watched a humanoid robot clean my apartment. It felt like a taste of the future.
